items.text: Entry. Anyone who joins a brand's newsletter list (site signup, checkout opt-in, or an import marked as new) gets the Day 0 welcome on joining, then the follow-up steps on their days.
Exit on purchase (your W01–W05 request). Any paid order of the brand, at any time, stops every remaining Welcome step. The check runs daily, so a step already sent isn't recalled.

Frequency Risk: Welcome and Thank-you on the same day. Someone who opts in at checkout on their first order currently gets BOTH the welcome and the first-order thank-you (last 28 days: ~20% of Thirsty Girl & ~10% of Ruze sign-ups got both messages back-to-back).
Recommended: Skip the Welcome and send only the Thank-you to someone whose signup IS their first order.

Frequency Risk: Monthly launch overlap (your W04 question). Nothing suppresses a broadcast for someone part-way through the Welcome series; they receive both.
Recommended: Keep the step emails distinct and evergreen (don't restate the month's launches in W04), so there is nothing to duplicate. That is the only practical way to maintain multi-brand, multi-language campaigns at this scale — for the people writing them even more than for the platform.

No restarts (your completion-tracking question). Every follow-up step sends once per person, ever — even if they unsubscribe and later re-subscribe. The one exception: the Day 0 welcome DOES send again on re-subscribe. That's deliberate today; confirm you want it.
Unsubscribing from the newsletter stops every remaining step of both series.

Ruze's 15-day step. Keeps sending as-is.
Recommended: The current campaign best fits the Day 2 “Gentle conversion reminder”: retire the 15-day campaign and re-schedule it as the 2-day step, without re-sending it to anyone who already received it.

Entry (your transition request). A customer enters on their first paid order EVER with the brand, only if they are subscribed to the newsletter at the time (ticking the checkout opt-in counts). Returning customers get no thank-you and no series. A buyer who isn't subscribed gets only the receipt — no marketing email.

The clock is the order date, not delivery. The step timings assume 5-day delivery.
Recommended: Start the clock at delivery instead. Aftership delivery confirmations would time "Getting started" and "How's it going?" to when the product actually arrives, so we never ask for a review of something still in transit. Orders with no delivery confirmation (untracked carriers, split shipments) fall back to order date plus 5 days, so nobody gets stuck.
Final step skipped for anyone who has ordered again since their first order. A repeat buyer never gets an earlier step late either.
Returning customers get no thank-you today. Do you want one?

Frequency Risk: Multiple brands. Overlap today is small: 4.7% (1,185 of 25,045 active newsletter subscribers) are on two or more brands' lists, and only 0.8% (205) on three or more. The industry pattern is a per-person cap by message class, with journeys and transactional email exempt.
Recommended: Add a per-person cap only if overlap grows past ~15%. For broadcasts, skip, never defer: someone who already got one brand's broadcast that day is skipped from the second brand's, not pushed to the next day, with the tiebreak going to the brand they engage with more. (Klaviyo Smart Sending skips the same way: 16-hour default, per account, no cross-brand awareness.)

Frequency Risk: Per brand. This is where the real frequency risk is (broadcast cadence + two series). A new non-buyer can get the welcome, three No-purchase steps and every broadcast the brand sends in their first 10 days — up to seven emails in ten days — and a new buyer gets the same shape from the New Customer series. Journeys alone are fine; it's journey steps stacking on broadcasts that creates the concern.
Recommended:
1. A "Smart Sending" rule, per brand, broadcasts only: skip a broadcast to anyone who received a journey email from the same brand in the last 24 hours. Journeys are exempt: one-shot and time-bound.
NOTE: A skip, not a defer. A listmonk campaign finishes and doesn't revisit, so there is no "tomorrow" to defer to. (Klaviyo Smart Sending skips too: 16-hour default, per account, no cross-brand awareness.)
2. Fix the same-day double (item 3): the one stack that hits every checkout opt-in.
3. Keep sunset as the backstop, and watch complaint rates in Brand Health: fatigue shows up there first.
Language. A campaign's language reaches that language only; English also reaches subscribers with no language on record.

Who it applies to. Every brand that sends from listmonk, each brand on its own: someone who stops engaging with one brand keeps getting the others. The check runs once daily, at 9:00 am Mountain (8:00 am in winter).

What counts as engagement. A click on any of the brand's emails, a paid order of the brand (whether or not an email drove it), or an open we can confirm was a person — today, an open through Gmail. Automatic opens (such as Apple Mail's privacy feature) and opens we can't confirm don't count; those subscribers are judged on clicks and purchases. Klaviyo does the same: clicks and placed orders count, and Apple privacy opens are excluded.

0–180 days: normal sending. This is the generous end of common practice (90 to 180 days, with 90 the usual starting point), so a subscriber gets twice the usual time before any hold. The stricter engagement definition (item 16) is what makes 180 days safe: automatic opens don't count, so nobody stays "engaged" without reading. 180 days is our starting point; if complaint rates in Brand Health rise, we will shorten it.

Hold at 180 days without engagement. When someone's last engagement (or their sign-up, if they never engaged) is 180 or more days ago and the brand has sent them at least 6 broadcasts since, they stop getting its regular sends. Every new engagement restarts the 180 days. This is a hold, not an unsubscribe: no opt-out is recorded, and they move to the brand's re-engagement list.

Two re-engagement emails, 90 days apart. Each ask is an automated journey, one per brand, in each language the brand's subscribers use. The first ask goes out the day someone is held; if they don't engage within 90 days, the last-chance ask follows, with another 90 days to respond. No one is suppressed without having received both asks. The Re-engagement circles above (180d, 270d) show each brand's journeys; the Sunset column shows whether sunset is set up.
⚠ Both journeys must be running, in every language the brand's subscribers use, before its first subscriber reaches 180 days. Without them, held subscribers get no emails at all and are never suppressed: they wait until the journey starts or they come back on their own. When the journey finally starts, everyone waiting gets the ask that same day — for a brand that has gone without one for a while, that is a large send to a cold audience, so plan it like a win-back send.

Coming back. Any engagement from item 16 (a click, a Gmail-confirmed open or a purchase) returns a held subscriber to regular sends the next day, with no new welcome email. Unsubscribing from an ask is a real opt-out: they are never asked again.

360 days: suppressed from marketing. After 360 days without engagement (180, then the two 90-day re-engagement windows), the person is archived for that brand: off its re-engagement lists and out of its marketing, but never deleted or blocked. Only their own action brings them back: signing up again, opting in at checkout, or re-subscribing on the preferences page.

Safety check. If a brand's latest broadcast shows zero tracked opens, that day's run skips the brand: broken tracking looks exactly like nobody reading. Holds for bounce problems are handled separately and never get the re-engagement emails.

rows: Regular sends stop; two re-engagement emails, 90 days apart
sunset-policy.note: *and at least 6 broadcasts received since then. Engagement means a click, a purchase, or a Gmail-confirmed open.
